# Andreas W. Neitzel

> PhD candidate in astronomy at IA/CAUP (Instituto de Astrofísica e Ciências do Espaço), University of Porto. Develops machine-learning methods for Galactic archaeology: manifold learning that separates the stellar populations of the Milky Way in chrono-chemo-kinematic data, and neural networks that infer stellar chemistry from *Gaia* XP spectra. First author of Neitzel et al. 2025 (A&A 695, A243), which validates a UMAP and HDBSCAN method on a synthetic Milky Way-like galaxy. Developer of the machine-learning pipelines of the FCT exploratory project ArqueoGal (2024.15303.PEX). Author of Starfold, an open-source Python package for label-free group recovery with reliability flags.

## Publications

- [Neitzel et al. 2025, A&A 695, A243](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202451718) ([arXiv:2501.16294](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.16294)): first-author paper introducing manifold learning (UMAP and HDBSCAN) for chemodynamic stellar-population separation on a synthetic Milky Way-like galaxy
- [Campante et al. 2024, A&A 683, L16](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202449197): co-author; solar-like oscillations in the K5 dwarf epsilon Indi with ESPRESSO
- [Magrini et al. 2022, A&A 663, A161](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243405): co-author; *Ariel* stellar characterisation of 187 FGK planet hosts

## Software

- [Starfold](https://github.com/AndreasWNeitzel/starfold): Python package, MIT, release 0.2.0 (2026-10-19); [manual](https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/Starfold/)
- [Stellar Explorer](https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/stellar-explorer/): browser app for a MESA r24.08.1 plus GYRE 1 solar-mass track
